newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium and copper drift from highs by LME close.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium and copper drift from highs by LME close.

text.p: Base metals by the end of Friday's London Metal Exchange (LME) trading fell back from their earlier highs, though traders said this was mainly due to end-week profit-taking and light broker liquidation.
Aluminium slipped from its earlier 3-1/2 month high of $1,535 a tonne, while copper drifted towards $2,200.
A tight physical market, recent investment fund buying and uptrending charts helped to underpin the aluminium market.
"Although it's below its highs aluminium has performed well on the upside, a move that may encourge fresh short-covering next week," one trader said.
Three months delivery aluminium was last at $1,530, against Thursday's $1,504 close.
Traders said aluminium's performance reflected investment fund shorts following forward selling last October.
They said a large proportion of aluminium stocks are tied up in long term financing deals and are not readily available to the market to alleviate the growing tightness.
A break above resistance at $1,540 next week could spark a move towards $1,600, some traders said.
"Noone is likely to run the market short at the moment," one commented. He said there could be fresh consumer buying next week.

Copper dipped from a high of $2,218 to settle at $2,208, down $4. Overall the copper market remained quiet and continued to consolidate. Traders will watch closely the LME stocks data next week on Tuesday and Friday.
Several are expecting inventories to rise after a long string of declines.
This would spark speculative selling, though traders believed substantial tonnages would have to be delivered into LME warehouses before a full scale sell-off emerged.
They also said that the strong backwardation present in the market could attract material into LME warehouses.
The cash to three months backwardation was last at $135/$145, versus levels of $40/50 that prevailed at the start of Novemeber.
Nickel on the back of buy-stops and despite an LME stocks rise snapped higher. It was last at $6,910, a gain of $40.
But given nickel's recent poor chart performance, which has seen prices down to a two-year low of $6,650 this week, several traders expect further downside pressure next week.
Other metals remained quiet. Zinc climbed by $4 to $1,080.
Lead was lsat at $710, down $3.
Tin settled at $6,115, against $6,160.
Alloy was at $1,370, against $1,345/50.
